_meta.purpose: One record per source behind data/size/<reference_id>.csv, plus records for databases that are only ever cited as the upstream of another (role 'upstream'). build_size.py refuses a row whose reference_id has no record here.
_meta.independence: independence_group says which sources share underlying data. Compilations copy each other: COMBINE took most bat masses from the Amniote database, which took most of them from PanTHERIA. A row's upstream_source names where its value came from; build_size.py follows that chain and, when the upstream row carries the same value, folds the copy into it ('also in ...') instead of counting it again.
_meta.basis: Every row is 'measured' (from real bats, by the source or a study it compiled) or 'estimated' (computed for a species nobody had measured: imputation, genus averages, allometry, or a parent species' value after a split). The page shows an estimate only when no measurement exists, and labels it as one.
_meta.same_as_calls: true means the citation, DOI, URL and licence are those of the record with the same id in data/calls/references.json, which already cites the work for its call data; only what is specific to the size import is written here.
_meta.licence_note: As for the call data: tables are committed only where the licence permits (CC0, CC BY). 'open-access-terms-unstated' sources contribute factual measurements, with the open licence question recorded rather than assumed away.
